meta.title: GCL Programming Language
meta.subtitle: A C-based, education-focused language designed for GnuchanOS.

sections.title: What is GCL?
paragraphs: GCL is a C-based programming language at the center of the GnuchanOS project. Its goal is to provide a simple and readable syntax for both education and game development.
It is written in small .c files, making the source easy to read and understand.
The current focus is GCL. Lua and Python support also exists (see #native ), but the current book chapters are for GCL.

notes.text: GCL is very close to C. If you know C, learning GCL takes a few hours.

sections.title: First Program
paragraphs: The simplest GCL program contains a main function and uses printf for output.
Note: GCL uses {} placeholders instead of C's %s / %d. Formatting supports syntax like {.2f}.
printf / scanf are built-in; you may also use the prefixed forms Stdio.printf / Stdio.scanf by declaring #native .

sections.title: Running
paragraphs: Save GCL files with the .gcsf extension. Then you can run them with:

code.src:
gcl -run file.gcsf
# Debug mode:
gcl -debug -run file.gcsf

sections.title: Vanilla C Types
paragraphs: GCL supports C's standard types: char, short, int, float, double, long int, long long int, long double and unsigned int.

sections.title: GCL Specific Types
paragraphs: GCL also provides its own fixed-bit-width and UTF-8-supporting types:

sections.title: Variable Declaration
paragraphs: Variables are declared as type name = value;. Multiple variables can be separated by commas.

notes.text: gcChar stores the real length for UTF-8 strings; it is not limited like C's strlen.

sections.title: Arithmetic and Assignment
paragraphs: Basic arithmetic operators are the same as C: + - / * %. Assignments can use += -= *= /=.

sections.title: Bitwise Operators
paragraphs: Bit-level operations: & (AND), | (OR), ^ (XOR), ~ (NOT), << (left shift), >> (right shift).

code.src:
int a = 0b1100;  // 12
int b = 0b1010;  // 10
int and_ = a & b; // 0b1000 = 8
int or_ = a | b;  // 0b1110 = 14
int xor_ = a ^ b; // 0b0110 = 6
int not_ = ~a;    // bitwise NOT
int left = a << 2; // 48
int right = a >> 2; // 3

sections.title: Comparison and Logic
paragraphs: Comparison: == != < > <= >=. Logical operators: && (AND), || (OR), ! (NOT).
Note: => syntax is also supported as >=.

sections.title: sizeof / strlen
paragraphs: sizeof() and strlen() functions are supported; sizeof()/sizeof() can compute array size.

sections.title: if / else if / else
paragraphs: Standard conditional statements are the same as C.

sections.title: switch / case
paragraphs: switch, case, default and break are supported.

sections.title: for
paragraphs: C-style for (init; condition; increment) loops are supported.

sections.title: while
paragraphs: while (condition) loops are supported.

sections.title: Function Declaration
paragraphs: Functions are declared like in C. Return type, name and parameters are specified.

sections.title: Scope
paragraphs: The global keyword makes a variable usable in a wider scope, while inline declares a local variable.

sections.title: const, public / private
paragraphs: const makes a value immutable. public variables are accessible from other files, while private is only valid in its scope.

sections.title: struct
paragraphs: struct can group data of different types together.

sections.title: typedef struct
paragraphs: typedef allows defining named structs. Here is the full struct example from simple_doc.md — it covers: empty struct + dot-assign, positional brace initializer, designated (.member = value) initializer, partial initializer, variable-based initializer, struct copy, empty + fill, and a struct returned from a function.

sections.title: enum
paragraphs: enum defines named constant integer values. It can be used both anonymous and with typedef.

sections.title: #define and #undef
paragraphs: #define defines constants and macros. Function-like macros are also supported.

sections.title: #if / #ifdef / #ifndef / #elif / #else / #endif
paragraphs: Preprocessor conditionals are supported. #if expressions evaluate arithmetic, comparison and logical operators; the defined() operator also works.

notes.text: #if expressions support both defined(X) and defined X forms.

sections.title: #warning / #error / #debug
paragraphs: Colored diagnostic messages are shown with #warning (yellow), #error (red) and #debug (blue).

code.src:
#warning This is a warning
#debug This is a debug message
#error This is an error message

sections.title: #native
paragraphs: The #native directive loads a module from .dll or .so files in the Library/ directory.

sections.title: #lib
paragraphs: #lib loads the Test.gclib library and its members can be called.

sections.title: #extern + #register
paragraphs: #extern loads an external DLL and #register registers C functions.

sections.title: #include
paragraphs: #include includes another GCL file.

sections.title: Loading and Core Window
paragraphs: The Raylib module is loaded with #native . It provides window, drawing, input and shape functions based on the raylib C library.
All colors are available as constants (e.g. Raylib.RED) encoded as 32-bit packed integers.

sections.title: Drawing
paragraphs: Core drawing functions: BeginDrawing / EndDrawing wrap the frame; ClearBackground, DrawRectangle, DrawCircle, DrawLine, DrawPixel, DrawText, DrawFPS and DrawRectangleLines are available.

sections.title: Input
paragraphs: Keyboard and mouse input functions return 1/0 for states.

sections.title: Shapes
paragraphs: Raylib.Rectangle(x, y, w, h) creates a rectangle value used by raygui widgets.

sections.title: Color Constants
paragraphs: All standard raylib colors are available as 32-bit packed integers.

sections.title: Loading and Core GUI
paragraphs: The Raygui module is loaded with #native . It must be used together with #native ; widgets read the last Raylib.Rectangle as their layout rectangle.

sections.title: Widgets
paragraphs: Available raygui widgets. Colored values are passed as 32-bit packed integers.

sections.title: Example: Button and Slider
paragraphs: A small window with a button and a slider. The button click resets a counter; the slider controls a rectangle width.

sections.title: Core Functions
paragraphs: The Math module is loaded with #native .

sections.title: printf / scanf
paragraphs: printf provides output and scanf provides safe input. They are built-in; the prefixed forms Stdio.printf / Stdio.scanf also work when #native is declared. Input is safer than C's scanf — no & or format scanner needed.

sections.title: File Operations
paragraphs: File functions support named arguments: file= and text=.

sections.title: Python and Lua Runtime
paragraphs: The Embed module starts, stops Python and Lua runtimes and provides variable sharing.

sections.title: Methods
paragraphs: Available methods and return values:

notes.text: The variable on the Python/Lua side must be defined in __main__ globals. Sent values are currently int, float, char and soon gcChar.

sections.title: New Project
paragraphs: The gcl -new project_name command creates a new project skeleton.

code.src:
gcl -new Demo

Demo/
    assets/       # automatically visible for raylib
    external/     # .so, .dll (gcl python lua searches here)
    include/      # .gcsf
    lib/          # .gclib
    out/          # Demo, Demo.gcBundle
    scripts/      # lua, python files
    main.gcsf
    project.gcdata

sections.title: project.gcdata
paragraphs: Project settings are stored in the project.gcdata JSON file.

code.src:
{
  "project_name": "Demo",
  "developer_name": "developer",
  "version": 0.100,
  "open_lua": true,
  "open_python": true,
  "single_bundle": false,
  "gcl_dirs": [],
  "gcl_scripts": [],
  "lua_dirs": [],
  "lua_scripts": [],
  "python_dirs": [],
  "python_scripts": [],
  "lua_main_file": "main.lua",
  "python_main_file": "main.py",
  "gcl_include_path": "include",
  "gcl_lib_path": "lib",
  "gcl_external_path": "external",
  "python_import_path": "scripts",
  "lua_import_path": "scripts",
  "raylib_asset_directory_path": "assets"
}

sections.title: Build
paragraphs: Project compile and package commands:

code.src:
# Run a single file:
gcl -run file.gcsf

# Run Python / Lua:
gcl -pyrun file.py
gcl -luarun file.lua

# Start IDE:
gcl -ide

# Build project:
gcl -build project.gcdata -o path/dir
#    -> Demo.exe / Demo.gcBundle

sections.title: Build Directory
paragraphs: Compiled output is collected under Build/OS_NAME/.

code.src:
Build/
    windows/
        Library/
            Math.dll
            Stdio.dll
            Embed.dll
            Lsp.dll
            Raylib.dll
            Raygui.dll
            Embeded/
                Lua_Runtime/
                Python_Runtime/
        Programs/
            ide.dll
        gcl.exe
    gnuLinux/
        Library/
            Math.so
            Stdio.so
            Embed.so
            Lsp.so
            Raylib.so
            Raygui.so
            Embeded/
                Lua_Runtime/
                Python_Runtime/
        Programs/
            ide.so
        gcl
